katas.title: Pricing: make a price version's end date inclusive so its last day is still billed at that price

seededDefectKey.scenario: A price change takes effect on 1 July: the old version is [Jan 1, Jul 1), the new one [Jul 1, open). Usage is billed for 1 July.
seededDefectKey.consequence: Both versions now apply on the changeover date, so PriceSelector.Select throws price.overlap and every invoice touching that day fails to price; the one-character change breaks the composition of adjacent versions.
Selection deliberately refuses to guess between two matches, so an inclusive end turns every changeover date into an ambiguity error instead of a price.
The shipped regression requires the boundary date to select the new version only; the sprint notes even name this exact one-character bug as the exercise.

katas.title: Tiered rating: rewrite the tier walk with inclusive "first unit / last unit" ranges

seededDefectKey.scenario: A tenant uses 150 units on tiers 100 @ $1 and remainder @ $0.50.
seededDefectKey.consequence: The next tier starts AT the previous tier's last unit instead of one past it, so the last unit each tier prices is priced again by the next: 150 units = 100 + 51 = $125.50 instead of $125. Any quantity that ends inside a tier with a tier after it gets a phantom 1-unit charge there (50 units bill $50.50, 100 units $100.50).

seededDefectKey.scenario: The inclusive arithmetic also changes non-boundary inputs.
seededDefectKey.consequence: Rating takes decimal quantities; anything below one unit (e.g. 0.5) now breaks out before the first tier and is rated at $0.

seededDefectKey.scenario: The repo already paid for this bug once.
seededDefectKey.consequence: The repair was to keep non-overlapping (previousLimit, upper] intervals; the patch re-introduces the overlapping fencepost.

katas.title: Payments: give each retry attempt its own provider idempotency key
katas.findingRef: meterforge-upskilling flaw harvest, Sprint 10 row (docs/quality/FLAW-HARVEST.md:11) and the duplicate-payment incident drill (docs/operations/INCIDENT-DRILL.md:3)

seededDefectKey.scenario: The provider commits the charge but the response is lost; the attempt is marked Failed and an operator (or job) retries it.
seededDefectKey.consequence: The retry reaches the provider under a key it has never seen, so it is a NEW charge rather than a replay: the customer is collected twice for one internal payment.

seededDefectKey.scenario: Why "failed" is not proof of non-execution.
seededDefectKey.consequence: Retry design must preserve the logical payment identity and reconcile provider state; a per-attempt key throws that identity away.

seededDefectKey.scenario: The shape of the type already says so.
seededDefectKey.consequence: Attempt number is the per-try counter; the key is the stable logical identity the provider deduplicates on (FLAW-HARVEST Sprint 10 repair: "preserve the logical payment key and increment attempt only").
